Thousands of families have been forced from their homes after the Euphrates River reached its highest level in years, triggering widespread flooding across eastern Syria.
Heavy rainfall across Syria and neighboring Turkey caused water levels to surge, overwhelming reservoirs and forcing authorities to release water from dams along the river system.
Entire neighborhoods in Deir ez-Zor were inundated, with homes damaged or destroyed and residents evacuating by boat. Floodwaters also swept away makeshift bridges and submerged vast areas of farmland.
Farmers say they have lost entire harvests, adding to economic hardships in a region already struggling with years of conflict and displacement.
The disaster has hit communities still recovering from fighting earlier this year, raising concerns about humanitarian needs and long-term recovery efforts.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
India's Aravalli mountain range, one of the world's oldest at billions of years, is under severe threat from decades of unregulated open-cast stone mining across multiple states. The mining has destroyed farmland, depleted water sources, and spread dust pollution, while activists warn that 27 percent of the range has already been lost. The Aravalli acts as a critical natural barrier between the Thar Desert and the fertile Gangetic plains, shielding the region — including New Delhi — from dust storms and heatwaves. A 2025 court order intended to strengthen protections has been criticised for creating legal ambiguity that may enable further degradation, with campaigners citing millions of dollars' worth of illegal mining in individual villages.

Al Jazeera's Imogen Kimber reports.

description:
The US Central Command says it carried out what it calls defensive strikes on Iranian drone facilities over the weekend, targeting Qeshm Island and the city of Goruk. 
CENTCOM says the strikes were in response to the downing of a US drone by Iranian forces in international waters. 
Meanwhile, Iran's Revolutionary Guard says it targeted a US base that was used to launch an attack on Sirik Island, near the Strait of Hormuz. 
The IRGC did not specify the location of the US facility. 
The claim comes as sirens were heard across Kuwait, with Kuwaiti media reporting that air defense systems are responding to missile and drone attacks. 
The IRGC says it shot down an MQ-9 drone last Monday and forced other US aircraft out of Iranian airspace. 
The back-and-forth has triggered mistrust between both sides while diplomacy continues behind closed doors.

Al Jazeera's Almigdad Alruhaid reports from Tehran, Iran.

description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has ordered the military to expand its invasion of Lebanon and attack targets in Beirut's southern suburbs, despite growing international condemnation. 
The order comes after Washington proposed a roadmap to end the conflict that called for Hezbollah to halt attacks altogether, with an implicit threat that otherwise Israel would no longer refrain from targeting the Beirut area. 
Since mid-April, intense bombing of Beirut's southern suburbs had stopped, allowing many people to return, but now residents are making their way out again.
Israel has also been bombarding towns and villages across southern Lebanon, including the city of Nabatieh, and has issued multiple forced displacement orders for people living there. The military has captured Beaufort Castle, a strategic hilltop giving the Israeli army a commanding view over vast areas of southern Lebanon. 
Following that capture, Netanyahu ordered troops to push even deeper.

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Thousands of families have been forced from their homes after the Euphrates River reached its highest level in years, triggering widespread flooding across eastern Syria.
Heavy rainfall across Syria and neighboring Turkey caused water levels to surge, overwhelming reservoirs and forcing authorities to release water from dams along the river system.
Entire neighborhoods in Deir ez-Zor were inundated, with homes damaged or destroyed and residents evacuating by boat. Floodwaters also swept away makeshift bridges and submerged vast areas of farmland.
Farmers say they have lost entire harvests, adding to economic hardships in a region already struggling with years of conflict and displacement.
The disaster has hit communities still recovering from fighting earlier this year, raising concerns about humanitarian needs and long-term recovery efforts.

Al Jazeera's Dmitry Medvedenko reports

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Shipping restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz are compounding an already severe humanitarian crisis in Myanmar, where farmers are struggling to afford fuel and fertiliser. Farmers report that 50-kilogram bags of fertiliser are now five times more expensive than before March, while the country imports 90 percent of its fuel and up to 95 percent of its chemical fertilisers from the Gulf. 
The World Food Programme warns Myanmar could see a 50 percent drop in fertiliser use, potentially cutting farming output by 15 percent. More than 90,000 people have been killed and nearly four million displaced since the military coup in 2021.

Al Jazeera's Perry Wilton reports from Myanmar.
